observations: _classify_operator_turn creates root_task_id = BacklogItem.new_id() before its merged front-door classify call.
BacklogItem.new_id returns uuid.uuid4().hex[:12], so this caller's generated root_task_id is a non-empty non-null string.

_classify_operator_turn conditionally includes that root_task_id in classify_kwargs when _front_door_classify accepts the parameter; the exact pinned _front_door_classify signature does accept root_task_id.
_front_door_classify forwards root_task_id into mgr.classify_front_door when it is non-null and Manager.classify_front_door accepts that parameter; the exact pinned method signature does accept it.
Manager.classify_front_door enters `with self._task_usage_scope(root_task_id)` before calling the inner front-door classifier whose run_exec closure performs the Manager backend gateway call.
Manager._task_usage_scope returns self._usage_context_factory(root_task_id) when root_task_id is truthy and a usage-context factory exists.

The exact non-memory runner constructor supplies Manager usage_context=self.task_usage_context. task_usage_context(mission_id) calls self._set_usage_context(mission_id) before yielding, and _set_usage_context stores the same mission_id as _active_usage_mission_id and propagates it to distinct role backends through set_usage_context.

Therefore, on this exact production Web/TUI classification path with an available Manager backend, the generated root_task_id is rebound as the same non-null mission_id before the first Manager classification backend execution and restored after the scoped call.
